critical_code_review_comments: server.py — `import asyncio` correctly removed (grep confirms no residual usage). pyflakes clean.

server.py ask_ai (~line 1871) and process_whatsapp_message (~line 2876) — `except Exception as e:` → `except Exception:` is semantically identical because `e` was already unused inside the block; the log message strings used constants, not `str(e)`. This is why pyflakes flagged them (unused local). No behavior change and no risk of masking a real crash beyond what was already the case. Regression suite proves ask_ai still returns a proper 200 answer and never 500s.

AskAI.js:18 uid() = Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)+Date.now().toString(36) — 12+8 chars of entropy; probability of two chat messages colliding within a single session is effectively zero. Good choice over crypto.randomUUID for older browser fallback, and it moves messages away from index-based keys so React can preserve DOM identity across re-renders.
AskAI.js:60 citation chip key `${c.type}-${c.title}-${ci}` — includes index as tie-breaker, so identical (type,title) pairs from the same citations array won't collide. Good.

WorkCoach.js:121,134 strengths/improvements keys `${prefix}-${i}-${it.slice(0,24)}` — the index is still in the key, which means the point of the content suffix is really just to make keys visually diff-friendly and stable if the array is re-ordered by a re-render. Fine.

ContactProfile.js:148 signal keys `sig-${i}-${s.slice(0,20)}` — same pattern; safe. Line 199 price-history key `${h.item||'row'}-${h.date||''}-${i}` — the falsy fallbacks are important because the raw upstream data can have missing item/date; without the fallbacks the key would be `undefined-undefined-<i>` which is still unique-by-i but ugly. Good.
